text:
maria: FYI noticed a p95 spike on chat.generate after yesterday's kernel selection rollout + new token-budget heuristics. baseline was ~210ms, now we're seeing 360-420ms for medium routes.

sam: thanks, can you paste the perf trace / profile? is it kernel or batching?

maria: quick dump below — looks correlated with increased microbatch counts and higher small-batch kernel invocations. KV hit rate also dipped on those routes.

```
observed: route=chat.generate tier=mid
p50 120ms p95 385ms p99 720ms
batch-size-dist: 1:62% 2:18% 4+:20%
microbatch-count: +48% vs baseline
kv-cache-hit: 68% -> 52%
kernel: fused-attn-v2 selected for seq<=512
sched: dynamic-token-budget v2 (min_tokens=8, target=64, scale_by_tier)
```

lee: interesting — if kernel pref is switching to a different kernel at small batch sizes, cost per-token may jump. also lower KV hits increase decoding work. can you run linux perf and nvprof on a repro?

maria: already ran a short perf sample on canary nodes (links below). main differences: more frequent kernel launches, higher kernel setup time, and GPU occupancy worse for batches of size 1.

perf-bot: trace link: https://perf.internal/runs/3345678901; flame: https://perf.internal/flame/3345678901

aj: two hypotheses: 1) the token-budget scaling by tier is too aggressive for mid routes so we often end up with many size-1 microbatches; 2) kernel-selector threshold for seq len and batch size ended up preferring a high-latency kernel for the small batches. either could raise p95.

tess: can we try reverting only the token-budget heuristic (v2) on a small canary to see impact? cheaper/faster than rolling kernel back.

maria: plan proposal: A) roll token-budget back for mid-tier (target=96 instead of 64) on 10% of traffic, B) enable kernel selector telemetry to log chosen kernel + batch-size, C) run a short perf job to capture nvprof traces for both canary and baseline.

sam: +1. also add a metric for "kernel-switch latency" per request and a KV-cache-hit sliding window by route.

lee: I'll add a quick patch to kernel selector to avoid choosing fused-attn-v2 for batches < 2 until we understand. We should gate behind an env flag.

infra-bot: deploy queued: token-budget rollback -> canary (10%) by tess at 3345678920.

maria: added an adhoc eval set: ~1500 requests covering mid-tier route shapes. I'll run after canary flips.

perf-bot: scheduled nvprof capture (200 samples) on canary nodes, ETA ~25m.

aj: if the rollback reduces p95 then we know heuristics were the main culprit. if not, kernel behavior + KV miss pattern likely root cause.

tess: canary is live now, monitoring. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/route/chat.generate/canary

maria: early numbers after 5m: p95 down to ~235ms on canary, kv-hit improved slightly (56%). still above baseline but much better.

sam: good signal. continue full 10% run for another 30m, then we can decide to keep change or iterate on kernel selector.

lee: I'll keep the kernel-selector flag ready; if canary doesn't hold we flip it. I'll also look into why kv-hit changed (prefetch/eviction?)

maria: assigning follow-ups: lee -> kernel selector flag + telemetry, aj -> expand route-level kv-hit metrics, tess -> monitor canary and roll-out plan, sam -> coordinate perf captures. I'll post results in ~60m. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: nvprof captures complete, artifacts uploaded.

maria: final note — this looks like an interaction failure between batching heuristics and kernel selection thresholds. we should add a regression test that simulates high single-token-request mixes so future heuristics don't regress p95.

sam: Agreed. creating ticket: INF-2187 "regressions: batching heuristics x kernel selector e2e test"

maria: thanks everyone, closing thread once ticket lands and canary finishes.
